'''Summon Raging Spirit''' (commonly referred to as '''SRS''') is a [[minion]] [[spell]] that temporarily summons a [[flying]] flaming skull that charges at enemies and [[attacks]] them.

==Skill functions and interactions==

* '''Behaviour:''' Raging Spirits move towards player's cursor when summoned, but otherwise do not follow or listen to the player. Enemies inside their aggro range will be attacked immediately. If multiple Raging Spirits are nearby, they will attempt to choose different targets, making them more effective in spreading their damage across an entire pack of monsters. Due to their flight and aggression, they are effective pack clearers when combined with {{il|Melee Splash Support}}.

* '''Duration:''' Each Raging Spirit has a base [[duration]] of 5 seconds. To reach the maximum of 20 Raging Spirits, investing in skill duration might be necessary to extend their lifetime. Additionally, cast speed, {{il|Unleash Support}}, {{il|Spell Echo Support}}, and added gem quality can be used to maximize their number and duration.

* '''[[Damage conversion]]:''' Raging Spirits deal base [[physical]] damage. Their {{c|mod|100% of their Physical Damage is converted into Fire Damage}} stat is inherent to the minion, not the summoning skill or its own attack skill, meaning it has the same priority as other sources of non-skill conversion like {{il|Triad Grip}}, {{il|Sidhebreath}}, and [[Unholy Might]]. The ratio is scaled down to 100% if the sum exceeds 100%. For example, wearing Triad Grip socketed with 4 green gems will cause 100% of Physical Damage to be converted to Fire and 100% to Cold, which is scaled down to 50% Fire and 50% Cold conversion.

* '''Cannot Be Targeted:''' Raging Spirits cannot be targeted directly, but they can be damaged by enemies accidentally, or through an [[area of effect]]. {{il|Summon Reaper}} cannot target them for consumption. Due to being invalid targets, they also cannot apply [[Taunt]]. 

* '''Flying:''' Raging Spirits are [[flying]] minions, which means they can move freely over terrain that characters would have to use a movement skill like {{il|Flame Dash}} to cross, such as cliffs, gaps, bodies of water etc. They are also unaffected by some [[ground effects]], and do not block the movement of non-flying entities.<ref>https://www.pathofexile.com/forum/view-thread/777516/page/1#p6740821</ref>

* '''Aggression:''' Raging Spirits have a naturally large aggro range. Making them [[Minion#Aggressive_and_Defensive|Aggressive]] (such as with the {{il|Feeding Frenzy Support}}) does nothing,<ref>https://www.reddit.com/r/pathofexile/comments/cu8vsc/what_minions_are_now_a_consideration_with_the_new/exwrafz/?context=4</ref> except cancel out '''Defensive''' if also supported by {{il|Meat Shield Support}}. 

* '''Convocation:''' Since Raging Spirits do not follow the character, they cannot be recalled using {{il|Convocation}}.

==Strategy==
===Sustaining Maximum Spirits===
The attributes that will improve max spirit count are [[Cast Speed]] and [[Skill Duration]].  Due to their short duration and very high maximum of 20, sustaining the maximum number of Raging Spirits is challenging without the use of a support gem.

{{il|Unleash Support}}, In conjunction with some improvements to Skill Duration from the tree, notably [[Enduring Bond]], will allow you to sustain the maximum number of spirits relatively easily, but at the opportunity cost of another damage improving support.

Between {{il|Unleash Support}}} and {{il|Spell Echo Support}}} The former is generally preferred as it allows the caster to remain mobile, and its damage penalty only applies "when Reoccurring" so immediately stops applying to the created Raging Spirits.



If we assume:
{{math|formula=
\begin{align}
D & \text{ percent increased Duration } \\
C & \text{ percent increased Cast Speed } \\
E & \text{ percent More Cast Speed } \\
\end{align} 
}}


And in a scenario where you can continuously cast Summon Raging Spirits without stopping, then the formula for how many spirits are on the screen at a time will be:

{{math|formula=
5.0 * ( 1 + {D \over 100} ) \over { 0.5 \over { ( 1 + {C \over 100} )  * ( 1 + {E \over 100} ) } }
}} which simplifies to: {{math|formula=
10.0 * ( 1 + {D \over 100} ) * ( 1 + {C \over 100} ) * ( 1 + {E \over 100} )
}}

And then round up to get the maximum number of spirits reached (with a maximum of 20).

Example calculation: If you have 45% increased skill duration, 76% increased cast speed, and 70% more cast speed, you would have {{math|formula=10 * 1.45 * 1.76 * 1.70 = 43.384 > 20}}, which means that if you continuously cast, your spirits will despawn earlier than necessary. This means you can spend several seconds per cycle on other things such as dodging, casting curses, or moving in between spirit castings.

Formula for {{il|Spell Totem Support}} (30% reduced cast speed, Spell Echo's More Cast Speed doesn't apply):
{{math|formula=
7.0 * ( 1 + {D \over 100} ) * ( 1 + {C \over 100} )
}}

===Scaling Damage===
Due to their relatively high effectiveness for added damage, especially considering their overwhelming numbers, Raging Spirits scale superlatively with sources of "flat" added damage.

Notable sources of flat added elemental damage include: {{il|Added Cold Damage Support}}, {{il|Added Lightning Damage Support}}, {{il|Immolate Support}}, {{il|Wrath}} and {{il|Anger}}

Due to the Raging Spirit's fairly low base damage, its remarkably easy to essentially "convert" their damage type to something else by adding enough flat damage of that type.

A popular strategy using these two points above is to add a huge amount of flat added [[Chaos]] damage to the Raging Spirits and then have them inflict [[Poison]] which allows for extremely efficient scaling of their damage per second through effects like [[Wither]] and the {{il|Temporal Chains}} curse.

Notable sources of flat added Chaos damage include: {{il|Added Chaos Damage Support}} especially from {{il|The Covenant}}, {{il|Chance to Poison Support}} and the special [[Envy]] aura, which can be found at its highest level from either {{il|Severed in Sleep}} or {{il|United In Dream}}.  

When not using {{il|Severed in Sleep}}, [[Wither]] chance for the spirits can also found with the {{il|Withering Touch Support}} which also adds a significant amount of Chaos damage but as a percentage of the Spirit's base Physical damage.

[[Ghastly Eye Jewel]]s also include mods for flat added damage of each type, as well as chance to poison.

==Version history==
{{Version history table header}}
{{Version history table row|3.24.0|
* The Raging Spirit's melee attack no longer naturally gains 0-38% more Damage as it levels.
}}
{{Version history table row|3.23.0|
* No longer has Minions deal 0-38% more Damage. Instead, the Raging Spirit's melee attack now naturally gains this damage scaling with level.
* Quality now provides 0-30% chance to summon an extra Minion, instead of 0-20% increased Minion Movement Speed.
}}
{{Version history table row|3.22.1|
* Added text to the Summon Raging Spirit Skill description to clarify that the Minions convert all [[physical]] damage to [[fire]].
}}
{{Version history table row|3.19.0|
* The damage and life scaling values for minions have been adjusted. Generally speaking, minion life and damage is unchanged in the very early game, roughly 30% lower in mid acts, roughly 20% lower at level 20 of the minion skill, and roughly 10% lower at level 30 of the minion skill.
* {{il|Summon Raging Spirit|Raging Spirits}} no longer has {{c|mod|Minions gain 15% less Added Damage}}. 
* Now has {{c|mod|Minions deal 0% more Damage}} at gem level 1, up to {{c|mod|38% more Damage}} at gem level 20 (previously 0%). 
* Minion base life is now 20% higher at all levels. 
* Now costs 4 mana at gem level 1 (unchanged), up to 16 at gem level 20 (previously 12). 
* The Helmet Enchantments that grant a chance to summon an extra Minion now grant a 16% chance from the Merciless Labyrinth (previously 12%) and a 24% chance from the Eternal Labyrinth (previously 18%). 
}}
{{Version history table row|3.16.0|
* Summoned Raging Spirits now convert all of their Damage to Fire Damage.
}}
{{Version history table row|3.6.0|
* <s>Mana Cost at gem level 20 is now 16 (was 12).</s>
* Raging Spirits, Raised Zombies, 'of the Grave' enchantment minions, and Spectral Spirits (from Essence of Insanity on a weapon) now have 100% more base accuracy rating than previously. Raging Spirits mana cost changes have been undone.<ref name="RecentlyAdded"/>
}}
{{Version history table row|3.1.0|
* {{il|Summon Raging Spirit|Raging Spirits}} now have a 15% less Added Damage multiplier, up from 30%.
* Raging Spirits, Spiders created from [[Arakaali's Fang]], and the spirit skulls from the {{il|Essence of Insanity}} can no longer taunt their enemies.
}}
{{Version history table row|2.5.0|
* Reduced the maximum number of Summoned Raging Spirits to 20, but we have also increased damage as the gem levels up to compensate. It's intended to be a similar damage output but with less casting needed and less effective area of effect.
* [[Totem]]s and all other minions now have 40% elemental resistance and 20% chaos resistance. This also includes minions that didn't have resistances previously, like wolves.
}}
{{Version history table row|2.1.0|
* Summon Raging Spirit's duration has been increased from 3.5 seconds to 5 seconds. The mana cost has been reduced from 6 to 5 at level one and reduced from 15 to 12 at level 20. The cast speed has been reduced to 500ms from 800ms. The damage dealt by Raging Spirits has been substantially reworked and is lower at high levels. Raging Spirits are now more likely to target enemies who are attacked by fewer Raging Spirits, except when enemies are close to the caster.
}}
{{Version history table row|1.3.0|
* Raging Spirits have had their damage reduced at higher levels. There's no change at gem level 9, scaling to 8% less damage at level 20 of the gem.
}}
{{Version history table row|1.2.0|
* The damage done by the summoned Raging Spirits has been reduced at higher levels, up to a 20% reduction in damage at level 20.
}}
{{Version history table row|1.1.5|
